title: Exponent as repeated multiplication
note: A power is repeated multiplication: a² = a·a, a³ = a·a·a, a¹ = a.

title: Coefficient vs. exponent
note: 2a means a+a; it is not a². (And a² = a·a is not 2a.) The two forms that look most alike mean the most different things.

title: Negative base vs. negated square
note: The exponent binds before the minus: -a² = -(a²), which is negative. That differs from (-a)² = a², which is positive. E.g. -3² = -9 but (-3)² = 9.

title: Exponent on a product
note: A power on a bracket applies to every factor: (ab)² = a²b², and (2x)² = 4x². Without the bracket, ab² means a·b² — the exponent hits b only.

title: Zero and one as exponents
note: Any nonzero base to the power 0 is 1: a⁰ = 1, not 0. And a¹ = a.

title: Negative exponent as a reciprocal
note: A negative exponent means reciprocal, not a negative number: a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ. So a⁻¹ = 1/a, and 1/a⁻ⁿ = aⁿ.

title: Fractional exponent as a root
note: A fractional exponent is a root: the denominator is the root index, the numerator the power.

title: Negative fractional exponent
note: Combine the two rules: a^(-m/n) = 1 / (nth root of aᵐ). The minus gives the reciprocal, the fraction gives the root.
